newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-TYSON AND HOLYFIELD TO GET $30 MILLION EACH FOR REMATCH.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-TYSON AND HOLYFIELD TO GET $30 MILLION EACH FOR REMATCH.

text.p: Evander Holyfield and Mike Tyson each will receive a guaranteed $30 million for their heavyweight title rematch next month, promoter Don King said on Wednesday.

There were reports in recent months that Tyson was to have received $5-$10 million less than Holyfield and that Tyson was upset with not receiving parity with the man who thoroughly beat him up before stoping him in the 11th round of their first fight November 9.
But in a telephone conference call on Wednesday, King said, "Mike is getting $30 million too."
King said the two fighters will share in the receipts from pay-per-view television for the June 28 fight if the sales exceed a certain number. He would not reveal that threshold.
The rematch had been scheduled for May 3, but Tyson suffered a cut in sparring and the fight was rescheduled.
"Team Tyson" -- as the men who handle the former champion like to refer to themselves -- say their man is in the best shape of his life.
Richie Giachetti, brought in after Tyson lost his World Boxing Association title to Holyfield, said he has returned to the methods of Tyson's first boxing mentor, Cus D'Amato.
"I am bringing Mike back to what he had when he had the title. We're just working on what he does the best and putting it together," Giachetti said.
Tyson co-manager John Horne said "one of our goals has always been to establish Mike Tyson as the greatest heavyweight champion of all time."
He said the rematch at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas will be a chance "to record why somebody is who he is, and Mike Tyson is without a doubt, especially in this era, the greatest heavyweight champion."
